the game/ebook
booyeah.
Title sequence plays the first time you load up the book. Pull out from one of Dickens Dean's screens.
We start off in Dickens Dean's bedroom office. He stands alone in the center of computer monitors. He is scraggly, neurotic. His workspace is his workspace.
He draws, paints, creates music, talks to friends half a world away, and does his thing.
His beautiful house sits atop a strange suburb transplanted to the edge of the Oregon coast, science fiction impossible but beautiful and tactile.
His daughter comes into the room, Dickens smiles and turns to her.
We don't see her yet. The hem of a yellow dress in the doorway, a hand on the frame.
Close on the nearest monitor. A text game he's been building for years, a cursor blinking at the bottom of the screen, waiting on him.
Baby girl, what are you doing down there?
Watching you go crazy.
I was working.
She mimics him, almost like a dance.
Working.
I forget you can't see yet, you're still too young.
But I can see, Daddy.
There's so much more out there, magic but a part of us. Here.
Dickens Dean hands her a pair of clunky old goggles, which he keeps in his desk.
He watches her face light up as she looks around the room.
Wow.
You're still too small. But you'll find your own way of seeing, when you're bigger.
I want to see more.
Dream of it, baby girl. Soon enough. Until then dream.
INT.
